transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Yeah, um… thanks. It’s probably not a huge thing, but I’ve noticed I’m kind of arranging my day around avoiding elevators. Like I’ll take five flights of stairs at my place, and I turned down a workshop because it was in a high-rise. I also stopped visiting one of my older computer students because his building doesn’t really have another option. I know that probably sounds a little silly, but it’s starting to get in the way.
Have you ever had a sudden panic attack in or around an elevator?

I don’t know if I’d call it a full panic attack exactly… but, yeah, there’s this sudden rush. Like as soon as I step toward an elevator or hear it clunk open, my chest tightens and my hands get sweaty. It kind of hits before I’ve even really thought about it, if that makes sense.
Are you mainly afraid of elevators themselves?

Mostly, yeah. I mean, I know logically an elevator in an office building is probably safe, and I’m not trying to be dramatic. But when I look at the older doors in my apartment building or at work, my brain kind of jumps to, “What if I get trapped?” or “What if it drops?” Even though part of me knows that’s probably over the top.
When you avoid elevators, is the main fear being in the elevator itself?

Yeah, I think so. It’s more the idea of being inside it, if that makes sense. I know an elevator in an office building is probably fine, but when I see those older doors in my apartment building or at work, my mind goes straight to, like, what if I get trapped in there, or what if it drops. I know that sounds kind of over the top, but that’s where my head goes.
Are you worried that people might watch you or judge you when you use an elevator?

No, not really. I mean, I might feel a little embarrassed if I look nervous, but I don’t think it’s about people watching me or judging me. It’s more just… the elevator itself, I guess. Does that make sense?
Have you ever had one of those sudden rushes of fear come on out of the blue, when you weren’t near an elevator or thinking about one?

I don’t think so, no. At least, not that I’ve noticed. It’s usually tied to seeing an elevator or knowing I’m about to have to use one. I haven’t really had it just come out of nowhere, if that’s what you mean.
